207.author: zhaozhaozz
207.body:
The Nightly on `dec6c686` ([run 36188684291](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/36188684291)) failed one journey: `journey-compact-process.spec.ts:138`, the check that a completed `run_shell` record has no border, expected `borderTopWidth` `"0px"` and received `""`. The same commit passed on the push CI ([35979748259](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/35979748259)) and on the previous Nightly ([36058461332](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/36058461332)), and `main` has not moved since, so this is a race in the test rather than a change in the product.

`""` is not a thin border. It is what Chromium returns for every computed style property of an element that is no longer in the document. The test read the card at the moment the page was replacing it.

## Root cause

Two things combine.

**A finished run's cards are mounted afresh.** A run is streamed into the live timeline, which `App` renders after the conversation blocks. Once it ends, the session refresh replays its persisted events and it is rendered inside the blocks, under `Fragment key="run-<id>"`. Those are different subtrees, so React mounts every card in the record and removes the live ones. A `MutationObserver` on the journey records exactly one removal of the completed `run_shell` record around completion, every run, and the removed node already carries `completed process-record` — exactly what the test's locator matches.

**`locator.evaluate` is two round trips.** In the pinned Playwright 1.61.1 it is `waitForSelector` to resolve an `ElementHandle`, then the function runs against that handle. The page keeps running in between.

Whether the hand-off lands before or after the API reports the run terminal varies. Locally it landed 500 ms before `waitForRunTerminal` returned, so the test only ever saw the record. The Nightly's trace shows the other order:

| UTC | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 20:58:46.508 | `toHaveClass(/process-record/)` starts, passes |
| 20:58:46.534 | page requests `GET /runs/<id>/events` — the replay that builds the record |
| 20:58:46.556 | `waitForSelector` resolves the handle to `<details class="timeline-disclosure tool completed process-record">` |
| 20:58:46.619 | failure screenshot; the handle's `getComputedStyle` read `""` in between |

Holding that replay in the browser and releasing it between the two steps `locator.evaluate` performs reproduces the Nightly's value on every run: `{"connected":false,"borderTopWidth":""}`.

## The fix

Replacing the `evaluate` with `toHaveCSS` alone is not enough. A web-first assertion queries and reads in a single evaluation, so it cannot see a detached node — but it would pass at once on the live card, which is also `0px`, and move the race onto the one-shot `boundingBox()` reads a few lines further down, which land right in the hand-off window by the Nightly's own timings.

The step has to measure the record, and nothing in the DOM told the two apart: the same `<section class="run-timeline">`, the same header, the same parent. So `RunTimeline` takes an optional `recordedRunId`, rendered as `data-run-record`, and `App` passes it for the record only. The step looks the card up inside `.run-timeline[data-run-record="<runId>"]`; its assertions wait for the record to exist, and every read after them is on a node that is not replaced again.

The `0px` check becomes `toHaveCSS("border-top-width", "0px")`, and so does the re-collapse check one step later, which is the same one-shot read of the same record. The expectation is unchanged.

The attribute is omitted when the prop is not passed, so the live timeline and the sub-agent conversation render exactly as before.

## Validation

Tested SHA: `ea392f7a8f607d9066ac69f0153eb0f635f8bdba`.

| Layer | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UT | `pnpm ci:ut` | PASS — 3170 planned / 3170 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped |
| ST | `pnpm ci:st` | PASS — 1/1 |
| E2E | `.ci/run-e2e.sh mocked` with `E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1`, as the tagged runner invokes it | 44 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (the existing `test.fixme` in `literature-review`); `check-e2e-meta` 48 spec files, 0 errors |

The five web test files that render `RunTimeline` (`RunTimeline`, `SessionRunTimelines`, `ProcessLifecycle`, `RunStopFlow`, `UiUsability`): 100/100.

## E2E user journeys

The journey this changes, `test/journey-compact-process.spec.ts:43`, run against an isolated stack started the way the E2E layer starts it:

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Natural timing, `--repeat-each=5` | every run passes | PASS 5/5 |
| Replay held 3 s, so the record mounts after the API reports terminal — the Nightly's order | record absent when the API says terminal; step waits for it and passes | PASS 3/3; record count at terminal was 0 in all three |
| Replay released between resolving the card and reading it, as `locator.evaluate` does | old read returns `""`; the fixed assertions pass in that same state | old read `{"connected":false,"borderTopWidth":""}` 3/3; fixed step PASS 3/3 |

The last two scenarios used temporary copies of the spec with a route holding the replay request; they are not part of this change.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`

User impact: none. The timeline renders identically; a finished run's record now carries a `data-run-record` attribute naming its run.

Compatibility and migration: none.

212.author: Birfy
212.body:
Fixes #210. This PR targets `feat/jiuwenswarm` and supersedes #211. The local memory graph now computes folded products by visiting each scope child once, so branching `next` paths cannot multiply the folded view's intermediate rows. It preserves the child identity used by surrogate edges and group expansion.

## Review follow-up from #211

- Share relationship-path prefixes with a compact immutable reference and a depth-first active-edge set. The interpreter materializes a relationship list only when the query reads that path; ordinary long-chain counts now succeed in linear memory. A payload budget still protects requests that actually return many full paths.
- Apply the same work, time, row, and collection budget to top-level and nested clauses, including `CALL`, `FOREACH`, `UNWIND`, `CREATE`, fixed-length expansion, aggregation, and writes. The statement rolls back on a budget error. This bounds the covered interpreter operations; it is not a process-level memory isolation guarantee.
- Put session and scope predicates inside node patterns for subgraph, scope expansion, and group expansion reads. The local property index now narrows candidates before charging query work, so unrelated historical nodes do not make a fresh session fail.
- Preserve `CypherBudgetExceeded` through write-route handlers so read and write endpoints return the same structured HTTP 503 (`memory_graph_query_limit`).
- Rebuild scope and temporal `next` edges by method, and keep subagent children out of the main temporal chain.
- Evaluate row-independent projection expressions once and reuse exported collection values across result rows. This lets the review query return all 4,000 rows while allocating only one copy of its repeated 4,000-element list. A cumulative per-statement element budget still guards genuinely distinct large collections before allocation, including `range()`, list concatenation, literals, slices, `collect()`, and result export; query logs include `collection_elements`.

## Reachability and follow-up to the new review comment

The HTTP service exposes fixed query endpoints, not a raw Cypher endpoint. Its internal local backend still executes production statements using `collect()`, `range()`, and list concatenation, with lengths that can depend on stored data. I included cumulative accounting in this PR because those existing statements can reach the same allocation mechanisms. The limit covers interpreter-created collection slots; it is not a universal process-memory cap or a bound on graph storage and arbitrary scalar strings.

On the reviewer's exact `UNWIND range(1, 4000) AS i RETURN range(1, 4000) AS xs` query, the previous `afc5d900` code was killed by a **128,000 KiB polling RSS watchdog** (observed **138,528 KiB**, no result, **95 ms total process time**) on the same macOS host. The updated `b11b77a1` code returns **4,000 rows × 4,000 values in 5.6 ms**, with **24,960 KiB peak RSS** and `collection_elements=12000`. A row-dependent variant (`range(i, i + 3999)`) still stops with `CypherBudgetExceeded` before materializing 16 million distinct elements; the exact repeated-value scenario completes. A caller that serializes all 16 million logical output values still incurs the corresponding output cost; the service has no raw Cypher response endpoint. This is a separate same-host comparison from the reviewer's Linux `RLIMIT_AS` reproduction; the local watchdog is not an OS-enforced limit.

## Validation

- Local memory graph suite on `b11b77a1`: 186 passed, 1 deselected (`test_legacy_artifact_id_constraint_dropped` requires Neo4j server constraints), 0 failed. It includes real relationship-path output, cycle semantics, long-chain counting, nested write rollback, fresh-session indexing, and write-route 503 responses.
- [Linux GitHub Actions CI on `b11b77a1`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/36287493403): UT **3,684/3,684 passed**, ST **2/2 passed**, mocked E2E **69/69 passed**; Docker image, both binary releases, and coverage also passed. The real E2E job is daily-only and was skipped by design.
- Native `pnpm ci:ut` on `afc5d900`: 3,680 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed; preflight `HOST_MISMATCH` because this host is macOS/arm64 and the shared plan requires Linux/amd64. The unmodified target branch has the same preflight result (3,670 planned / 0 executed). The Linux CI run is the authoritative full layer.
- Native `pnpm ci:st`: 2 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed for the same `HOST_MISMATCH`; unmodified target branch: 2 planned / 0 executed.
- Native `pnpm ci:e2e`: 69 planned / 0 executed / 0 passed for the same `HOST_MISMATCH` after browser preparation; unmodified target branch: 69 planned / 0 executed.

### Before/after memory and query time

These are local measurements in separate child processes over in-memory synthetic graphs, with a 25-second timeout and a polling RSS watchdog. The watchdog kills after observing a threshold; it is not an OS-enforced address-space limit. Peak RSS includes Python and the graph; the delta starts immediately before the query. A terminated run has no completed query time, so the time shown for it is total child-process time to the watchdog, including graph setup.

| Scenario | Before | After on `b11b77a1` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18 branch/rejoin diamonds, folded view | `feat/jiuwenswarm` `acc660b2`: no result; RSS passed 256,000 KiB at 1.97 s total | 57 nodes / 75 edges in **3.1 ms**; peak **32,176 KiB**, query delta **+256 KiB** |
| 7,001-node linear path, `RETURN count(b)` | old PR #211 `b39fcd9f`: no result; RSS passed 128,000 KiB at 0.83 s total | count **7,001** in **31.0 ms**; peak **47,824 KiB**, query delta **+5,472 KiB** |
| 20,001-node linear path | old PR #211's smaller 7,001-node case already exceeded 128 MiB | count **20,001** in **108.7 ms**; peak **76,544 KiB**, query delta **+15,616 KiB** |
| 40,001-node linear path | old PR #211's smaller 7,001-node case already exceeded 128 MiB | count **40,001** in **272.5 ms**; peak **119,872 KiB**, query delta **+29,648 KiB** |
| New empty session with 125,001 unrelated historical SearchNodes | old PR #211 `b39fcd9f`: budget error in **253.9 ms**; peak **149,504 KiB**, delta **+240 KiB** | empty graph in **1.4 ms**; peak **148,160 KiB**, query delta **+112 KiB** |

The implementation reuses the existing indexed graph and Python standard-library iterators and data classes. Adding another graph library would duplicate graph storage for this read path, while enumerating all distinct paths can still grow combinatorially.

## Problem and behavior

Two completed real E2E runs delivered artifacts but failed scoring because the Judge spent its entire output budget on reasoning: BiomniBench DA-13-3 repeat 3 (8,192 tokens) and the PUCT supplementary audit repeat 2 (32,768 tokens). Increasing the budget to 65,536 recovered scores of 77 and 86.25 respectively on the first attempt. This PR brings that experiment's recovery policy into the test engineering code.

- Give Biomni and the optional PUCT Judge 65,536 output tokens and up to three retries after the initial request. Reuse identical evidence/rubrics and accept the first valid score; never select the highest score.
- Retry incomplete/invalid responses and transient transport errors, but stop on permanent HTTP errors such as authentication or insufficient balance. Retain the request body without credentials, each returned response, and attempt status/usage/timing in an immutable attempts directory.
- Allow 900 seconds per request and a separate configurable 65-minute scoring stage so the parent test does not kill recovery early. Agent execution budgets and delivery assertions are unchanged.
- Add the previously external PUCT supplementary audit as an opt-in repository entry point (`E2E_PUCT_LLM_EVALUATION=1`). 222.body:
## Summary

**Draft — do not merge until the full UT/ST/browser-E2E gates and remaining integration acceptance checks below are completed.** The implementation is available for review; targeted validation passed, but full local validation is incomplete.

Extract Idea Tree from the evolve process into an independently runnable Python service and expose its research capabilities as session-scoped MCP tools. This is the service-extraction work for #101 (part of #84), establishing a separate lifecycle and state boundary before the evolve migration in #102.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`. The candidate is `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e` (one commit; 45 changed files, including detected moves).

## 1. Independent service and state ownership

- Move `idea_tree_service`, `research_service`, the research engine, tree models, prompts and templates from evolve's vendored implementation into `services/idea-tree/src/sciencediscovery_idea_tree`.
- Remove both router registrations from the evolve server. The new package has no imports from evolve; the existing research algorithm is preserved rather than rewritten as part of the extraction.
- Add a dedicated FastAPI entry point, health endpoint, locked dependencies, shutdown cleanup and service-only authentication. Standalone startup fails closed without `SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`.
- Use a dedicated state root (`SCIENCE_AGENT_IDEA_TREE_DATA_DIR`, defaulting under the shared data root's `idea-tree` directory), atomic JSON persistence and independently persisted research settings.
- Copy legacy tree/research records on first startup without deleting originals. A migration marker prevents re-importing stale legacy data; conflicting destination records fail startup instead of overwriting data. Import the old API catalog's settings once, then keep settings authoritative in the service.
- Serve persisted skill references so skill deletion-impact checks include autonomous research as well as historical trees and chat-run references.

## 2. Service-owned MCP tools and capability isolation

The service publishes four tool contracts:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_idea_research` | Start autonomous research with an objective and prepared evidence/materials |
| `get_idea_research` | Query the current session's research and findings |
| `control_idea_research` | Pause, continue or end research |
| `view_idea_tree` | Read a historical tree graph |

The trusted control plane provisions a five-minute capability using its service credential. The scoped MCP endpoint supports initialization, discovery, calls, ping, notifications and revocation. Project/session identity and model callback credentials come from that trusted scope, not model-supplied tool arguments. Continue grants are pinned to a specific research ID. Expired scopes are rejected, active scope count is bounded, and revoking a transport scope does not terminate autonomous research. Access logging is disabled for this process to avoid logging capability URLs.

The API obtains schemas from the service and contributes them to the existing JiuwenSwarm MCP bridge/native executor. The former hard-coded create/get tool definitions in `packages/evolve` are removed. Tool discovery failure does not prevent unrelated chat tools from being used.

## 3. TypeScript client and unchanged frontend interfaces

- Replace `services/api/src/idea-tree/python-client.ts` with `IdeaTreeServiceClient` in `packages/idea-tree`. The client provides authenticated, bounded HTTP transport, dynamic tool discovery, scoped MCP research calls, settings transport and historical-tree reads.
- Route active research through the independent service rather than evolve. Preserve the research-created event, create-time chat messages and SSE forwarding.
- Keep historical compatibility types/read transport in `packages/idea-tree`; legacy mutating `tree_*` tools remain disabled.
- Preserve all six frontend paths and their existing response shapes:

| Interface | Handling after this change | Contract mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Research service command/query | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | Independent research lifecycle; control plane retains chat-message creation | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:researchId/events` | Independent service SSE, forwarded through the existing public route | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` | Historical graph read from independent storage | Existing `idea-evolve-memory-reads` |
| `GET /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned settings | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |
| `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` | Service-owned partial update, preserving values on an empty update | New `idea-tree-settings-noop` |

These are contract-case mappings, not a claim that a full baseline/candidate L1 differential run passed. The committed lifecycle golden fixture records the stable `running → paused → paused after restart → completed` projection and is asserted by the service journey; it is not a complete chat/agent event-stream golden trace.

## 4. Startup, packaging and test discovery

- Provision/start the new service through `scripts/start-stack.sh` and include it in the Docker image.
- Default to loopback port `4314`; reserve `4414` for the isolated browser-test stack and include it in busy-port checks.
- Add `pnpm idea-tree:test`, relocate the existing Python tree/research tests with the service, and include the service in tagged test discovery, environment preparation and coverage roots.
- Add standalone-service documentation covering configuration, migration and the remaining control-plane boundary.

## Compatibility, migration and scope boundaries

- Stop the old stack before upgrading. The maintained startup script/Docker packaging includes the new process; custom process supervisors must launch it and provide matching service URL/token configuration.
- Run one ASGI worker: background research tasks and short-lived scopes are process-local. Research and settings are persisted; the journey verifies recovery of paused research after restart.
- The adapter still reaches these frontend routes through the existing API control plane. Session ownership, chat-message writes and model-secret provisioning are **not** moved into the new service by this PR.
- Research still uses the existing run-bound LLM callback pending #102; it does not receive provider API keys. Extracting the service does not remove that callback dependency from the wider stack.
- Prepared evidence is preserved, but this PR does not implement the artifact/provenance/CAS service tracked by #98 or change its ownership.
- This PR does not claim completion of the broader JiuwenSwarm migration or the full #101 integration acceptance matrix; full public-route differential and chat/agent trace verification remain review/validation follow-ups.

## Validation

Tested candidate: `8374ac7f6159a475b4743de5da276c8019b2774e`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm build` | PASS, recursive workspace build |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS, including test TypeScript configuration |
| Independent-service Python suite | 34 passed |
| `packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts` + `packages/idea-tree/src/client.test.ts` under Linux | 11 passed |
| `node test/contract/run.mjs --coverage` | Mapping check passed: 151/254 repository interface rows mapped; not 151 executed tests |
| `bash -n scripts/start-stack.sh` and `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh` | PASS |
| `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` | PASS |

Full local gates were attempted in separate checkouts of the candidate and unmodified upstream baseline `5de0ff59`:

- **UT: BLOCKED / incomplete.** `pnpm ci:ut` remained in JiuwenSwarm dependency preparation, downloading/building its Python dependencies, before the shared test runner started. The candidate attempt was manually stopped after approximately ten minutes in this layer; the baseline attempt was also stopped while in the same preparation stage. Both wrappers then recorded exit code 2 (`JiuwenSwarm could not be installed`). This is an interrupted preparation attempt, not an observed product assertion failure, and it does not establish that UT would fail on a fully provisioned host. No frozen plan or planned/executed/passed test summary was generated; those counts are unavailable, not zero-pass success.
- **ST: incomplete, with one smoke passing.** Both checkouts built successfully. The first attempts failed before planning (`A revision is required`) because WSL Git could not resolve the Windows-created temporary worktree metadata. After repairing only that metadata, both retries froze two identities. The candidate's native agent-loop smoke group reports **planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 1 / failed 0 / skipped 0**; the baseline emitted the same smoke's pass event. The other identity, `swarm-sdk-contract`, requires JiuwenSwarm setup, which was still preparing dependencies when the run was stopped. No complete two-identity ST summary is available. The retries reused the exact SHA's completed install/build via `CI_E2E_PREPARED=1`; no test selection was removed.
- **Browser E2E: incomplete / not executed.** `pnpm ci:e2e` was invoked on both candidate and baseline; preparation reached the pinned `.e2e` dependency installation after the workspace build. The attempts were stopped during preparation. No browser plan, executed-journey count or final summary was produced. This is not a browser PASS and not evidence of a candidate-specific failure.

Remaining local verification was deliberately stopped rather than leaving background preparation jobs running. The draft status reflects these incomplete gates; a fully provisioned Linux/CI run is still required. The initial worktree metadata error was a local harness issue, not a source change; the dependency preparation attempts do not support claiming a pre-existing upstream product defect.

## E2E user journey

**PASS** — one independent-service API/CLI journey, seven numbered steps passed, zero failed/blocked/skipped. The driver launches the installed product CLI in a separate process, with an owned data directory and a local HTTP model stub; no paid model calls or external research services are used.

Command, from the repository root after installing the service:

```sh
services/idea-tree/.venv/bin/python test/api/idea-tree-service-journey.py
```

| Step | Expected and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Discover tools and save settings | Four MCP tools exposed; settings accepted by the independent process |
| 2. Start research with prepared evidence | Research enters `running`; the real engine reaches the local model callback |
| 3. Pause active research | Paused state persists; the delayed model response does not advance the paused stage |
| 4. Restart the service | Paused research and saved settings are recovered |
| 5. Read from another session | Cross-session capability cannot access the research |
| 6. Continue and consume SSE | 19 snapshots received; research completes with independently assessed candidate score 7; no model token in frames |
| 7. Check references and delete owned research | Persistent skill reference detected; owned session research removed |

This service-level journey does not substitute for the full browser stack, public API/JiuwenSwarm integration or a live-model test. Docker/release-binary execution was not locally verified.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature`

User impact: research is hosted in a dedicated service with explicit MCP lifecycle controls and persistent, independently owned settings/state. Existing frontend paths remain stable.

The contributor has read-only access to upstream (`push: false`, `triage: false`), so the GitHub `release:feature` label is **pending a maintainer**; it has not been applied.

The release branch `releases/v0.3.0.beta` should no longer get a daily build. It never had one of its own: GitHub evaluates `schedule` only on the default branch, so the cron in the release branch's `nightly.yml` does not fire. It was built daily because `main`'s scheduled Nightly carried a `dispatch-release` job that ran `gh workflow run nightly.yml --ref releases/v0.3.0.beta` on every scheduled run, starting a second, independent Nightly with that branch's own workflow and source. This removes that job and the documentation that describes it.

## Changes

`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`

- Removes the `dispatch-release` job, including `RELEASE_REF: releases/v0.3.0.beta` and the `actions: write` permission it was the only job to request.
- Removes the header's statement that the scheduled build also dispatches an independent run for the release branch. The header now says the workflow is the scheduled build of the default branch, and that any other branch runs it only when dispatched by hand at that ref.

`.ci/README.md`, *Daily real-E2E prerequisites*

- The scheduled Daily covers `main` only. The paragraph no longer says each scheduled run dispatches a run at `releases/v0.3.0.beta`; it says a daily gate for another branch runs only when someone starts `Nightly` with `workflow_dispatch` at that ref, using that ref's own workflow and source.

Unchanged: `schedule` with `cron: "0 16 * * *"`, `workflow_dispatch`, and the `stamp`, `gate` (`profile: daily`, `secrets: inherit`) and `report` jobs. Manual `workflow_dispatch` at any ref is deliberately left available. Nothing on the release branch is modified; with no dispatch from `main` and no schedule of its own, it simply stops receiving scheduled runs.

## Verified diff

Checked on this branch, based on `main` at `90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `git grep` for `dispatch-release`, `RELEASE_REF`, `releases/v0.3.0.beta` | no matches anywhere in the repository |
| `git grep` for `gh workflow run` | one match, a generic example in `.agents/skills/ci/references/github.md` that dispatches `ci.yml` by hand; nothing dispatches to the release branch |
| Jobs in `nightly.yml` after the change | `stamp`, `gate`, `report` |
| Triggers | `schedule` (`cron: "0 16 * * *"`) and `workflow_dispatch` |
| `gate` | still `uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `profile: daily` |
| README vs workflow | both state the schedule builds `main` only and that other refs run only by manual dispatch |
| `actionlint` on `nightly.yml` and `ci.yml` | clean |

The job being removed was added in a single earlier commit that touched only these two files, so nothing else depended on it, and no test or script reads `nightly.yml`.

244.body:
The `github` and `create-github-pr` skills both show `--head "$login:<branch>"` for opening a pull request. Under zsh, a letter right after that colon can be read as a modifier on `$login` (`:c`, `:h`, `:t`, `:r`, `:e`, and `:f` followed by one of them), so filling in the example for most branch names sends GitHub a head that is not the branch. GitHub answers with `No commits between …` and `Head ref must be a branch`, and the Troubleshooting entry for that message explained it only as a branch deleted after a merge. bash does not treat the colon specially, which is why the example looks correct.

## Changes

- Both examples now read `--head "${login}:<branch>"`, which bash and zsh expand the same way. `create-github-pr` keeps a one-line comment in the code block saying why the braces must stay.
- The `create-github-pr` Troubleshooting row for `No commits between` / `Head ref must be a branch` now gives both causes and how to tell them apart:
  - the branch was deleted when an earlier pull request from it merged — `git ls-remote <fork> 'refs/heads/<branch>'` is empty;
  - zsh mangled the head string — the branch exists, but the head echoed in the error no longer contains the whole branch name.
- The `github` skill has no Troubleshooting section, so it gets one sentence beside its example pointing to that row instead of a second copy that could drift.

Unchanged: placeholders such as `<login>:<branch>` and the gitcode skill's `<gitcode-login>:branch` are not shell expansions. No other skill puts an unbraced shell variable directly before a colon in a command.

## Validation

Each skill's `gh pr create` code block was executed verbatim in GNU bash 5.2.21 and zsh 5.9 (`zsh -f`), with `gh` and `git` stubbed so that `gh api user` returns `octocat` and `gh pr create` prints the `--head` it received. Only the angle-bracket placeholders were filled in. Nothing was sent to GitHub.

Before (the blocks as they are on `main`), identical for both skills:

| Branch | bash | zsh |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chore/skill-zsh-head` | `octocat:chore/skill-zsh-head` | `octocathore/skill-zsh-head` |
| `fix/e2e-border` | `octocat:fix/e2e-border` | `octocat:fix/e2e-border` |
| `feat/release-notes` | `octocat:feat/release-notes` | `at/release-notes` |
| `release/v0.3.0` | `octocat:release/v0.3.0` | `octocatelease/v0.3.0` |
| `e2e/compact-process` | `octocat:e2e/compact-process` | `2e/compact-process` |

After: all 20 cases (2 skills × 2 shells × 5 branches) print `octocat:<branch>` with the branch intact.

`fix/` surviving is not a counterexample: `:f` only acts when the next letter is itself a modifier, and `i` is not. Which names break depends on the letters after the colon, so a spelling that worked for one branch proves nothing about the next — the Troubleshooting row says so.

247.author: zhaozhaozz
247.body:
When a finished model response carried a tool call whose arguments did not parse, the JiuwenSwarm model gateway rejected the whole turn. JiuwenSwarm never received the call, did not retry the model request, and the run or subagent failed, often after 20 to 40 minutes of completed research. The page then said "The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration", although the provider had answered normally. On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) this ended DRB-64 (main run, after 23 minutes) and twice killed the TC-E2E-01 delivery-signoff subagent, the first time after its MCP check had already returned `ok: true`. Fixes #236.

The failure was on the ScienceDiscovery side, before Swarm saw the call. JiuwenSwarm's pinned agent-core would have returned the parse error to the model as a tool result, and the native runtime already does (`INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS`, `retryable: true`). Only finished responses on the Swarm path were fatal: truncated ones already went through bounded output-limit recovery.

## Withhold the response and let Swarm's recovery ask for the call again

`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`: for a task turn that finished normally but has a call with `argsParseError`, the gateway now withholds every call of that response, appends `[invalid_tool_arguments:tool_calls_withheld]` with the tool names and parser messages, and finishes the response with `length`, exactly as it already finishes a cut response. Valid sibling calls are withheld too, so a response is either executed whole or not at all. V8 quotes an input excerpt in some `JSON.parse` messages (`Unexpected token 'c', ..."command": cat secret"... is not valid JSON`); that excerpt is removed, so no argument text reaches the notice. The private diagnostics file still records the full message.

`jiuwen_swarm/patches/workswarm0.2.6/0007-output-recovery.patch`: the existing per-instance recovery wrapper recognises the marker, classifies it as `invalid_tool_arguments`, and adds `[Tool argument recovery N/2; invalid_tool_arguments]` feedback that names the failing call and asks for one valid JSON object (escaping, smaller pieces for long text). It shares the existing budget of two extra model calls and raises the same structured `output_recovery_exhausted` error on exhaustion. The gateway reads the attempt back from that feedback; the two sides now point at each other where the `N/2` budget is shared.

Why withhold instead of returning an error: Swarm does not retry an error the gateway raises at the end of a response. By then the response is a 200 stream, so it arrives as an SSE `error` event, which neither the OpenAI SDK retries nor agent-core's recovery hooks (context overflow, stream stalls, tool-call loops) cover. Why not pass the call through to Swarm's own argument repair: the gateway re-serialises calls from parsed arguments (`toolCallsOf`), so the tool would run with `{}`; the adapter's platform-tool stream rewriter parses complete arguments at `finish_reason` and would end the stream; agent-core's bracket-balancing repair can turn an incomplete call into an executable one, which patch 0007 already avoids for cut responses; and the unparseable string would be replayed to the provider in later history. A withheld response is never replayed, so none of these layers see it.

## Only where every requester can recover

The recovery wrapper is installed on the run's own Swarm instance. With `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_SUBAGENTS=jiuwenswarm`, Swarm's native sub-agents send model requests through the same gateway without it, and agent-core takes a `length` response without tool calls for a final answer: the sub-agent would have returned the notice as its result, and the parent's next request would clear the failure. In that mode the gateway keeps failing the request, as before. The default `task` mode runs every sub-agent as its own platform run with its own wrapper. Housekeeping calls (titles, compaction) also keep failing, since they have no wrapper.

## A run never ends silently on a withheld response

`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`: if Swarm ends normally right after a withheld response, the run fails instead of completing. When recovery is exhausted, the error reads `Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell) after 2 recovery attempts; gateway request chatcmpl-…`. The withheld-response notices (this one and the existing `[output_limit:tool_calls_withheld]`) are cut from the text shown to the user and from the run transcript; the adapter forwards every chat delta, so before this they appeared in the assistant's message.

## Name the failure instead of blaming the model configuration

`invalid-tool-call` is a new `RunFailureCode`. `classifyRunFailure` checks it first, because the tool names in the message are arbitrary and could contain words such as `transport`. The Web UI shows "The model wrote a tool call whose arguments could not be read, so it was not run and the run stopped. Retry the task; if it keeps happening, try another model." (and the Chinese equivalent) instead of the configuration hint.

## Let `setup` upgrade an install whose patches were revised in place

Patch 0007 is edited in place, as 0005 was in 94f98bbc; a separate patch on top would break the installer's idempotent re-apply. On a source install made before such an edit, `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` used to stop with `output_recovery.py: already exists in working directory`, while `start` told the user to run setup. `scripts/swarm-patches.py apply` now compares the recorded patch set with the current one; when they differ in a source checkout, it first returns the patched paths to the pinned tag (removing files that patches created) and then applies the whole set. Wheel and site-packages targets are always built fresh and are unaffected.

## Validation

Local host with bubblewrap. ST and E2E ran on this head's tree (`fcbb8730`). UT ran while the head was `dbdd402d`, which differs only in `scripts/swarm-patches.py` resolving a relative `--patch-dir` and in the ST-only installer test.

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3710 | 3710 | 3709 | 1 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- The one local UT failure is `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts` › "a blocked run holds its Session queue until the user decides permission" (`queued work did not overtake a blocked run in the same Session`, `2 !== 1`). It is pre-existing on this host: on unmodified `main` (`9189206d`), the same case run alone under `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` (as the layer runs it) fails with the same assertion. The GitHub Actions UT layer passed it on `ed849f6f` (3705/3705).

## Summary

- Add a shared E2E helper that follows a foreground Run through main-Agent background Executions and automatic wake Runs before checking final delivery. A completed foreground Run alone does not mean that its background work is finished.
- Use the helper in the Biomni, DeepResearchBench, and Research Team real E2Es. It selects only the root and subsequent main-Agent wake Runs as delivery candidates. Any active Run in these isolated Sessions, including a child Run, blocks settling because the notification dispatcher cannot admit a main wake while a Session Run is active. Main-Agent executions and pending timers also block settling; failed polls restart the quiet window.
- On generation budget expiry, stop the Session wake gate before cancelling active Runs, shell executions, and timers. Re-read Runs and activity until shutdown is verified or one cleanup deadline expires. Record `stopped`, `cleanup_failed`, or `unverified` without treating a failed read as an empty Session. Biomni and Research Team distinguish budget expiry from polling/API failure, retain partial artifacts, and fail the overall E2E on budget expiry.
- Read declared Artifact versions from the current main-Agent Run chain. For each declared Artifact, use its newest version on the current main-Agent Run chain; an acknowledgement-only wake can inherit earlier output, while a broken newer version of the same Artifact cannot fall back to an older one. The final E2E gate also checks each benchmark's requested handoff, so an intermediate note alone cannot pass.
- Add deterministic tests for deferred execution, child Run dispatch blocking, late wakes during cleanup, timer/execution cancellation, failed reads, cleanup deadline exhaustion, and versioned Artifact delivery.

Addresses #252. Related to #233, which concerns displaying the product error after an E2E delivery assertion fails.

## What the live scenario shows

I ran one focused browser E2E against an isolated ScienceDiscovery Web/API/Runner/JiuwenSwarm stack. A local scripted model made the sequence deterministic; it did not call an external model or Jina. **The E2E passed (1/1).** The screenshots are product UI states, while the Run and Execution completion states were also checked through the API. This scenario demonstrates why the E2E harness must wait beyond the first foreground Run; it does not claim that the product lifecycle itself is broken.

Read the screenshots from left to right: **the central chat shows the user's messages and agent replies; the right `Workspace → Executions` panel shows the background task's state.** The same background Execution is followed throughout.

1. **First Run ends; work continues.** In the center, the agent says “This turn is finished.” On the right, `local · main` is still **running**. Checking final artifacts at this point would be too early.

   ![Step 1: the first reply says the turn is finished, while the Executions panel still says running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/01-run-ended-execution-running.png)

2. **A new user question is accepted while the same Execution runs.** The center shows the second message and its reply; the right panel still says **running**. The browser submitted the message through the normal composer, and the two user Runs both reached `completed`.

   ![Step 2: a second user message receives a reply while the earlier Execution is still running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/02-new-run-completed-execution-running.png)

3. **The background Execution and automatic wake Run finish.** The right panel now says **completed**. The API confirmed Execution exit code 0 and the automatic wake Run at `completed`. On this still-open page, the chat had not shown the runtime notice after about 10 seconds. This is a separate UI refresh observation, not a behavior changed by this test-only PR.

   ![Step 3: the Executions panel says completed, but the live chat has not yet shown the runtime notice](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/03-wake-completed-before-reload.png)

4. **Reload reveals the persisted result.** The center now shows `RUNTIME NOTICE: Synced 1 background execution result(s)` and the wake reply. The scripted model uses a fixed reply, so its wording is not the subject of this test; the ordering and delivery state are.

   ![Step 4: after reload, the chat displays the persisted runtime notice and wake reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wyhohyw/sciencediscovery/042f20a541f45809325a28f808b9a3861326b919/docs/evidence/issue-252/04-execution-finished-wake-notice.png)

The [issue #252 reproduction note](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/252#issuecomment-6095525545) has the same evidence and the separate UI observation. The screenshots are stored on an independent evidence branch in the contributor's fork; they are not part of this PR's code diff.

## Versioned Artifact delivery

The E2E reads declared versions from `/api/sessions/:id/artifact-outputs` and attributes child versions to the parent main Run. It selects the newest declaration **for each Artifact ID and logical name** across the current main Run chain. A later wake declaring `notes.md` keeps an earlier `trace.md` and `answer.txt`; a newer declaration of `answer.txt` replaces only that file. The selected newer version must be readable and nonempty: a broken version cannot fall back to an older version of the same Artifact. Versions from unrelated earlier Session Runs do not count.

Each real benchmark then checks its own required deliverables: Biomni requires `trace.md` and `answer.txt`; Research Team requires `evidence_brief.md`; DeepResearchBench keeps its official report name unless a later Run explicitly hands off another file as the final report. A casual reference to `notes.md` cannot replace the official report. An explicitly handed off renamed report is recognized with sentence-ending punctuation and relative paths such as `./results/review-v2.md`. Required artifact checks prefer a main-workspace declaration over a `subagents/<id>/` copy; without a main copy, they use the latest producing Run and leave same-Run ties ambiguous. Biomni scoring reads the same selected trace and answer versions. A broken supplementary draft remains in delivery diagnostics without failing otherwise valid required outputs. The final chat reply is retained for diagnostics and, for a renamed DRB report, checked against the report's own producing Run. Intermediate files alone cannot satisfy the benchmark. Scientific quality and rubric scoring remain separate.

## Validation

- Original implementation head `9deabda`, rebased onto `main` `e9eac41`: WSL `pnpm typecheck`, 41 focused delivery/Run-chain/shutdown/scoring tests, `pnpm docs:lint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Poll-timeout follow-up at head `7a572ff` (rebased on `main` `e7ba5c9`): one Playwright read timeout is retried within the existing three-failure budget. The pure `run-poll-recovery.unit.ts` tests error classification; a mocked browser E2E in `journey-deliver-result.spec.ts` exercises `waitForRunChainTerminal` after a timed-out read. The earlier placement of this integration test in the UT suite caused CI collection to fail because that runner does not provide `@playwright/test`; the test is now in the Playwright suite. The previous local helper tests (38/38), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm docs:lint` passed before this relocation; `git diff --check` passed on the new head. A fresh local dependency install was blocked by missing offline registry metadata. Hosted UT and the new mocked Playwright regression pass. The mocked standard-config group timed out once in an unchanged compaction journey, then passed 19/19 on a targeted rerun; `merge-gate` passed. A code-identical single-commit refresh at head df03896 re-triggered the hosted gates: CodeCheck (GitCode), L1, UT, ST, all four mocked E2E groups, Coverage, and merge-gate passed. Real E2E was skipped by the PR workflow.
- The three helper suites are named `*.unit.ts` and tagged for the shared UT plan. The CI Node collector loaded all 35 tests in those files (22 delivery, 8 Run-chain, 5 shutdown); a full local UT slice was blocked by the local paper virtualenv missing `pytest`.
- Four isolated mocked browser E2Es passed after the rebase, before the final report-handoff refinement. That refinement passed the focused unit tests. The mocked cases exercised the J2 versioned delivery journey, an acknowledgement-only final reply, the background-execution notice, and localhost-only browser traffic. No external model or Jina calls were made.
- New deterministic tests cover a wake adding unrelated notes, a wake revising only one required file, an empty optional draft, a broken newer required version, renamed Artifact identity, report handoff across Runs, a later wake casually mentioning `notes.md` after the official DRB report, and punctuated/relative-path handoffs of renamed reports, and main-versus-child copies of required outputs.
- Prior real-model run on the pre-follow-up head: Biomni DA-13-3 and DRB-59/62 passed; Biomni DA-14-1 exhausted its configured 20-minute budget. These runs used the user's direct DeepSeek API with quality scoring disabled and no Jina key. Real-model cases have not been rerun after this Artifact selection follow-up.

This PR changes the E2E harness only. It does not change the product Run/Execution lifecycle. Biomni journeys remain outside the daily gate until the separate nightly-restoration PR is merged.

Cumulative CI tiers now separate inexpensive PR feedback from reviewed real-model execution. L1/L2 run on each PR; the merge queue reruns the inherited checks and adds L3 basic real API journeys and distribution gates on the merge-group SHA. Daily and version builds use cumulative L4/L5 profiles; their current case sets and evaluation modes are equal. ## Behavior - Keep test cases orthogonal to `backend`: JiuwenSwarm is the default; `legacy` explicitly selects the native loop. Unsupported capabilities fail instead of silently changing case IDs or switching backends. - Keep a stable `merge-gate`, frozen source identities and exact `planned == executed == passed` accounting. Maintainer review plus enqueue authorizes the credentialed run; no separate Environment reviewer or final approval is added. - Remove L3 request/token spending caps and the proxy-imposed output limit. Retain provider usage, an explicit count of unreported calls, cancellation, transport guards and test timeouts. - Start L5 with the existing eligible suite: L3/L4/L5 contain 7/17/17 real cases. L4 retains all ten previously eligible nightly cases; L5 currently uses the same cases and evaluation modes, with its separate extension point preserved. L5 keeps existing assertions and AI score artifacts without requiring a historical regression baseline. It still blocks Release/assets when selected tests fail or results are missing. - Preserve the two Biomni and one seeded literature-review quarantine tags already present on main since `8bd4560d`. They remain outside automatic selection; release no longer downloads their unused datasets. Broader coverage and baseline calibration are follow-up work. - Isolate test JiuwenSwarm registries, workspaces and processes beneath each runtime directory while preserving normal product startup defaults. 261.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.

266.author: zhaozhaozz
266.body:
Closes #263.

A cancelled, timed-out or killed E2E job kept no diagnosable evidence even for journeys that had already failed. Playwright wrote `test-results/` outside the uploaded results, and `.ci/run-e2e.sh` copied it there only in its exit trap, which a cancelled job is killed before finishing. The `list` reporter prints errors only when the whole run ends. And journey reports record only errors raised inside `journey.step()`, which the benchmark journeys do not use. In nightly trial run 38107013490, three DRB journeys had failed before the run was cancelled, and none of the uploaded files said why.

## Per-test evidence is written into the results as each test ends

`run-e2e.sh` exports `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR=<layer results>/test-results`, and `test/playwright.config.ts` uses it as `outputDir`, falling back to `.e2e/test-results` when it is unset, so local `npm --prefix .e2e` runs are unchanged. Traces, failure screenshots, `error-context.md`, `benchmark-metrics.json` and the other per-test files are therefore in the uploaded directory the moment their test ends. The exit trap now copies only the HTML report, which Playwright renders once the run ends anyway. Each shared-runner batch already gets its own results directory, so Playwright clearing `outputDir` at start cannot wipe another batch's evidence.

## A failed journey says why, in its report and in the log

- A journey report whose test failed without a failed step gets a **失败原因** (failure reason) section with the test's own error. It goes through the same redaction and truncation as step errors, now also stripped of terminal color codes.
- When a journey fails, the lines that say what failed are printed right after its `journey report (FAIL)` line: the assertion message and expected/received, at most 6 lines of 300 characters each, redacted and without the stack. This is what the job log was missing, since the `list` reporter prints the same detail only at the end of the run.

The text handling lives in `test/helpers/test-failure.ts`, which has no Playwright import, so the unit layer can test it.

Not in scope: for a cancelled layer, the shared-plan summary still says "no frozen plan reported … the layer stopped before it collected its tests", because the shared runner writes its accounting only after Playwright exits. With this change, a cancelled run can be diagnosed regardless.

## Validation

Run locally on aa0af5a1 with a fresh `HOME`:

- **UT** (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 3716, executed 3716, passed 3716. This includes the new `test/helpers/test-failure.unit.ts` (3 tests) and the extended `run-e2e.sh` contract test in `.ci/ci-contract.test.mjs`, which now asserts that Playwright receives `E2E_OUTPUT_DIR=<layer results>/test-results`. With the export removed, that test fails (0 / 2).
- **ST** (`pnpm ci:st`): planned 2, executed 2, passed 2.
- **E2E, mocked** (`pnpm ci:e2e`): planned 70, executed 70, passed 66, failed 4. The four were LR-08, `journey-local-token-onboarding` (en), J6 model settings and `journey-session-trajectory`, failing on 10 s visibility waits (LR-08, trajectory), an alert still shown after 10 s (onboarding) and the 180 s test timeout (J6). ## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。

- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

Replace the L3 numeric/MCP probes with seven real-model user journeys adapted to ScienceDiscovery's public product interfaces. The same cases and assertions run with `--backend jiuwenswarm|legacy`; backend choice remains independent of case selection.

## Coverage

Every case below uses a real LLM and the local product stack, browser and public HTTP API. None uses a model stub or an LLM judge.

| Case | User task | Required outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `response` | Ask for a short streamed response | Actual content/reasoning deltas, a normal stop, a completed Run and nonzero per-Run input/output usage |
| `tool` | Read an uploaded file containing an undisclosed random marker | A real `run_shell` result and the final answer both contain the marker |
| `files` | Update one file while preserving its neighbour | Downloaded target bytes match the requested edit; neighbour bytes remain unchanged |
| `memory` | Reopen a Session and continue the conversation | Persisted history is available, the next request carries it, and the reply recalls the random code |
| `artifact` | Deliver an artifact and continue chatting | The same artifact version and content remain readable after another turn and reopening |
| `workspace` | Edit a relative path in one of two Sessions in the same Project | The other Session's same-named file remains unchanged |
| `cancel` | Cancel after actual model output, then continue | The Run becomes cancelled, the next turn completes, and no queued/running Run remains |

The transparent proxy counts meaningful stream deltas and finish reasons; role-only and keepalive frames do not count. Usage assertions apply to each completed Run, so title-generation usage cannot mask a missing task usage record.

L1/L2 remain unchanged. L3 still selects 7 cases; L4 and L5 each select those 7 plus the existing 10 research cases (17 total). When any one of the settings requests fired at startup or on opening System settings fails (for example `GET /api/memory/settings`), the model connect card loses its whole provider preset list. The provider select then displays "Custom provider" while the card still holds the DeepSeek selection, so the provider name / Base URL / model ID fields never appear, and picking "Custom provider" again does nothing because the select already shows that option. A freshly deployed instance with one misbehaving endpoint therefore cannot configure a custom model at all. Reported on the GitCode mirror as [openJiuwen/sciencediscovery#137](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/issues/137); tracked here as #281.

## Load the provider registry on its own (`App.tsx`)

`client.listProviders()` sat inside the same `Promise.all` as about a dozen unrelated settings requests, both in the startup batch and in the batch that runs when System settings opens. `Promise.all` is all-or-nothing, so a failure anywhere discarded the presets that had loaded fine. The registry now loads in its own promise in both places. Its errors go through the same reporting as before (the System settings alert, or the page error outside System settings), so a failure is still visible. Only the provider list is decoupled. The other settings stay in their batches, because they belong to the same panel and keeping them all-or-nothing is intended.

## Keep the wizard's selection consistent with the options it shows (`ModelConnectWizard.tsx`)

A React controlled `<select>` whose value matches no option makes the browser display the first option, and choosing that displayed option fires no change event. Decoupling the request fixes the reported trigger, but the same mismatch comes back whenever the preset list is empty, arrives late, or drops the selected preset. The wizard therefore now resyncs when its selection is no longer offered:

- It falls back to the first preset still offered, or to custom mode when there are none, so the select and the fields always describe the same choice.
- Custom mode entered only because no presets existed gives way to the first preset once presets arrive. It does not do so if the user has started filling the custom fields, or picked "Custom provider" themselves.

## Validation

GitHub Actions on this pull request ([run 38383509722](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/38383509722), head `84fdf2f7`) is green: L1, UT, ST, all four mocked L2 E2E shards, coverage, and the merge gate passed. CodeCheck on the GitCode mirror passed as well.

- **UT** (`pnpm ci:ut`, non-root): planned 3760 / executed 3760 / passed 3757 / failed 3. None of the 3 failures is caused by this change, and none of them failed in the Actions run above:
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts` › "the run's trajectory is recorded from the model calls JiuwenSwarm makes…" fails with `one turn: the title call is not one` (expected `context.captured` / `state.committed`, got only `model.completed`). This is pre-existing. It fails the same way 2/2 on unmodified `main` `e7ba5c92`, and this PR has no diff under `services/`.
  - `services/api/src/server.test.ts` › "Agent-created Skill stays in draft until review publishes it to a Skill Library" failed once with `0 !== 1`, then passed 3/3 when rerun alone on the same commit. This looks flaky.

## Summary

Add all **132 DeepResearchBench II tasks** as a release-only L5 benchmark, following the existing tagged Playwright real-E2E framework. L5 now selects **151** real cases (19 inherited + 132 DRB II); L4 remains 19. No new paid cases enter PR/L2 or merge/L3 gates.

## Design and scope

- Statically declare every task identity; collection is offline and cannot silently shrink when data or credentials are absent.
- Each task receives an isolated research worker through the existing matrix/reconciliation path. Preserve original task text and blocked-source instructions; only append artifact delivery instructions. Rubrics are never research-Agent input.
- Do **not** carry over the experimental two-subagent prompt cap. Product quotas still apply and are recorded. Memory Graph is disabled for DRB II workers.
- Download upstream only at execution time: `imlrz/DeepResearch-Bench-II@b38f360603db9531b102aef8c166cedb8509b6f6`, shallow/blob-filtered/sparse checkout of necessary files, locked Python dependencies, and dataset/evaluator hash checks. No upstream dataset or report corpus is vendored. Verified local `.git` size was about 708 KB.
- Reuse upstream rubric prompts and scoring; add strict response completeness/type checks and a non-destructive JSON parser (upstream's repair regex can corrupt valid compact JSON).
- Account for upstream task 116's duplicate rubric texts: 56 raw entries / 50 distinct scored entries, matching upstream text-keyed output rather than making the task fail permanently.
- Record reports, rubric results, per-call Judge usage including retries, model/config identity and separate generation/evaluation durations. Delivery/evaluation failure fails the case; valid low scores are review evidence, **not** hidden failures or an invented quality threshold.

## Configuration and release impact

Uses the existing `nightly-ci-ds` generator/Judge settings. `DRB2_JUDGE_API_STYLE` defaults to `openai`; set it to `deepseek` for DeepSeek transport. Judge output starts at 32,768 tokens and increases on truncation up to 65,536. One Judge request at a time, 15 rubrics per batch, at most three attempts.

Generation budget: 120 minutes/task; evaluation: 30 minutes/task; existing research job ceiling: 240 minutes including preparation. The workflow retains two concurrent jobs. At 30 minutes generation/task, DRB II alone is approximately 66 worker-hours / 33 wall-clock hours, before setup and judging. **A tag-triggered release now incurs this full paid benchmark and waits for its gate.** A timeout is not a spending cap.

DRB II workers do not require DRB I, HF or Jina evaluator prerequisites. Configured research providers may separately require keys. Per-task upstream licenses still apply, notably CC BY-NC for tasks 26 and 110.

## Verification

- CI contract suite: **59/59 passed**, including new selection/sharding, prompt isolation, score completeness and mocked Judge transport tests.
- L1: **4/4 passed**.
- Actual offline Playwright collection: **151 release identities**, exactly **132 DRB II**; daily remains **19**.
- Runtime shallow/sparse preparation and pinned checks: passed.
- Local transport smoke against the **actual pinned upstream evaluator and all 132 task rubrics**, with a synthetic loopback Judge: **132/132 passed**, no LLM tokens. This proves evaluator plumbing, **not research quality**.
- E2E metadata check: 0 errors (existing legacy warnings unchanged).
- Documentation checks, lint of modified runbooks, and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Explicit limitations / not claimed

- Full 132-task paid Agent execution was **not** run as part of this PR. Prior local four-report real experiments are not a full-suite result and are not this branch's E2E verification.
- No historical quality regression threshold and no claim of official leaderboard comparability; Judge model and execution conditions matter.
- Existing session token summaries can omit intermediate/child calls and are labelled **not a billing total**. Judge calls have their own detailed usage ledger.
- This PR does not fix the existing 5-second status-poll recovery policy, long-task resource pressure, or persistence performance. Failures remain failures; assertions are not relaxed to hide them.

295.body:
Startup and opening System settings loaded most of their data with `Promise.all`. One rejected request discarded every sibling that had already succeeded, so a single unhealthy endpoint blanked unrelated panels. #288 pulled the provider registry out of that batch. This change settles every read in both batches on its own, and puts the provider registry back in the same list. A failure is reported for that read only. A successful empty body is still applied, so an empty configuration stays different from a failed read.

## Settle each settings read (`App.tsx`, `settings-loads.ts`)

The two lists stay where they were. Each read applies or reports as soon as it returns, so a request that is still pending cannot hold back the ones that already succeeded. The aggregate promise resolves only after every read has settled. Callers use it to know the batch finished. The project sidebar and the address bar do not wait for that promise: `projectsLoaded` becomes true when the project list itself settles, including when that read fails. A successful empty body is still applied, so an empty configuration stays different from a failed read.

Opening System settings covers providers, models, connectors, skills, skill libraries, global settings, timeouts, quotas, sandbox network, web, memory graph, and idea tree. Startup adds projects, the model catalog, proxy settings, MCP proxy policies, and MCP sources. The reviewer-specialist read was already independent and stays that way.

With `GET /api/memory/settings` returning 500, or still pending, the provider presets, the model list, and global settings are still applied once those reads return. A failed or hung memory read no longer leaves the registry on "已添加 0/1" and "未配置" while those other reads have already succeeded, and it no longer leaves `globalSettings` unset for that reason.

## Preserve overrides when setting the default model (`default-model-override.ts`)

`onDefaultModelSet` used to copy `globalSettings` from memory. That copy is empty when `GET /api/settings` failed or has not returned, so the following `PUT` was only `{ modelId }` and `replaceGlobalSettings` replaced the stored overrides. The callback now reads `GET /api/settings` immediately before the write and changes only `modelId`. If that read throws, nothing is written. The registry's default-model row uses the same helper.

The wizard reads settings before it creates a provider or a model. If that read fails, it stops and reports the error; it does not create a row that the server would pin as the default and then refuse to delete. When the read succeeds, a later failure still writes that snapshot back before deleting the rows this attempt created. The registry default-model menu reports a rejected save through `onError` instead of leaving the promise unhandled.

This covers #291: connecting the first model after `GET /api/settings` returns 500 keeps `enabledConnectorIds`, `semanticReviewEnabled`, and `thinkingEffort`, and does not leave a new provider or model behind.

## Validation

Focused runs in WSL:

- `apps/web/tests/settings-loads.test.ts`: 6 passed / 0 failed. One rejected read does not discard fulfilled siblings, and an empty success is still applied. With memory settings rejected, both the System-settings list and the startup list still apply providers, models, and global settings. The startup list also still applies projects. A memory read that has not returned yet does not block providers, models, global settings, or the project-list settled signal. A rejected project list still marks projects settled.
- `apps/web/tests/startup-projects.test.tsx`: 1 passed / 0 failed. With `GET /api/memory/settings` still pending, the mounted App shows the project in the sidebar and moves the address bar to `/projects/project-1`.
- `apps/web/tests/default-model-override.test.ts`: 3 passed / 0 failed. Setting the default model keeps the overrides from the fresh settings read, clearing it removes only `modelId`, and a rejected settings read does not call the replace.
- `apps/web/tests/ModelConnectWizard.test.tsx`: 31 passed / 0 failed. A failed settings read does not create a provider or write settings. Without a callback, the first model is merged into the overrides returned at save time.
- `apps/web/tests/ProviderModelList.test.tsx`: the default-model menu reports a rejected save through `onError` and keeps the previous selection. The file's 14 tests passed.
- `services/api/src/store.test.ts`: rolling back the first provider model restores the previous global settings, then deletes the model and provider. Reopening the store still has those settings and no leftover rows.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed.

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not re-run on this host for this commit. The previous full runs here were on a 7.7 GiB WSL VM and did not finish cleanly (UT refused to run as root, the mocked E2E thrashed, and a research-suite download stalled on PyPI). Those layers are left to this pull request's Actions run.

## E2E user journeys

Not run for this commit. The user-visible paths are: one settings endpoint fails at startup, the same failure happens again when System settings opens, and connecting the first model after `GET /api/settings` fails keeps the other global overrides. Expected: every sibling that returned 200 is shown, the failed read shows an error, an existing model plus its global default stay visible, and the default-model write contains the overrides from a fresh settings read. The unit tests above check the load lists and the write body; they do not open a browser. #288 already ran the custom-provider journeys for the case where the preset list itself was missing.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: A failing settings endpoint no longer blanks the settings panels that loaded successfully, and setting the first default model no longer replaces the other global overrides when the settings read failed.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #290
Closes #291
Refs: #288

Also retain the original large-workspace, installer and usage-accounting fixes. Related to #283 (L5 scope); the private upstream tasks remain excluded.

## Public-50 execution and reporting

- Pin the dataset to `e1c8ca5e11a620087bc48d97888eb69176a1f235`; verify paths, sizes and checksums, preserve nested input formats and keep rubrics/reference answers outside the research workspace.
- Preserve the task instruction and retain the submitted prompt, including the research-team/multiple-subagent supplement. This requests the workflow without claiming that every skill/subagent actually ran.
- Keep AMD64 as the default and allow explicit ARM64 execution without duplicating the 50 tasks. Validate actual architecture, candidate SHA, dataset/evaluator/model/backend identity and required measurements.
- Publish `biomni-gate.json` and `biomni-gate.md`, including **every selected task**, completed/incomplete status, delivery/evaluation states, available score/token/RSS/time/tool-call/round measurements and structured failure codes. The real-report GitHub step summary includes the same task table and aggregate threshold outcomes.
- All 50 tasks need valid delivery, evaluation and complete required measurements. Missing/duplicate/incompatible records fail closed. Partial means are diagnostic, never a smaller-denominator certification. A valid zero score stays visible.

## Temporary A3 baseline and aggregate gate

The checked-in policy now uses **`mode: temporary`**. The two complete operator-supplied A3 result sets receive equal weight. Their mean score is 67.73, rounded to the agreed target 67.7. This is a provisional operational reference to recalibrate on the formal environment, not an approved identity-matched capability baseline. `non_regression_certified` remains false in temporary mode.

| Metric | A3 Excel actual | A3 v2 actual | Temporary baseline | Warning | Block |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean score, all 50 tasks | 66.80 | 68.66 | **67.7** | **<=64.7** | **<=62.7** |
| Total generation + judge tokens | 186,187,274 | 204,012,150 | **195,099,712** | **>=224,364,669** | **>=243,874,640** |
| Total tool rounds | 1,956 | 2,128 | **2,042** | **>=2,655** | **>=3,063** |
