| P95 of task peak RSS, GiB | 15.803780 | 6.599500 | **11.201639801** | **>=13.441967761** | **>=14.562131741** |

Boundaries are inclusive, with blocking taking precedence. Resource thresholds are independent: tokens +15%/+25%, rounds +30%/+50%, research duration +20%/+30%, and memory increase max(20%, 1 GiB)/max(30%, 2 GiB). The implementation compares unrounded values; integer count limits above round up. Memory P95 uses linear interpolation, calculated separately for each historical run and then averaged for the baseline. Keep the suite maximum visible; **131.07 GiB on A3 v2 `da-17-5` is an unresolved outlier, not an accepted normal maximum baseline**.

The operator reported large per-task score spreads (maximum 76 points). Therefore temporary mode gates the **50-task mean**, not individual score drops. Low scores and resource breaches do not trigger automatic retry-until-green. Absolute case budgets/timeouts and completeness checks remain separate.

The final-result scope matches the historical A3 summaries: one final valid research result and its selected evaluation per task, excluding earlier failed attempts. Sources are `BiomniBench-L5-50-A3-监控指标.xlsx` and `biomni-l5-50-A3-监控指标-v2.csv`; the latter mixes 39 initial results, 5 regression results and 6 reference results across revisions. These are diagnostic inputs, not new paid validation of this PR head. The generation/judge splits are 185,333,947/853,327 and 203,191,614/820,536 tokens; total tool calls are 2,068 and 2,305; maximum RSS values are 31.262096 and 131.07 GiB.

Additional incomplete references remain outside baseline calibration: WSL mean 65.95 over 40 scored tasks, known tokens >=6,747,892, 1,924 rounds and 787.11 research minutes over 41 recorded tasks, maximum complete sampled RSS 14.354 GiB. CPU mean 64.45 over 38 scored tasks, 9,652,680 recorded tokens, 1,922 rounds, 1,350 research minutes and 7.58 GiB maximum complete RSS. Token accounting differs across old/new runs; these values must not be pooled into the A3 baseline.

Explicit candidate mode remains available for an unapproved complete result set, and the existing approved identity-matched compare mode remains for compatibility. No run automatically approves or replaces a baseline.

## Non-blocking serial recovery: three additional retries

`test/benchmarks/biomnibench-da/suite.py` finishes every unattempted task before starting deferred retries. Preparation errors, process failures, resource-check failures and malformed per-case metadata are recorded with reasons; they do not abort subsequent tasks. Per-case inactivity/overall deadlines prevent one stalled task holding the rest indefinitely. Execution remains serial, not unbounded parallel work.

- **Research/delivery failure:** end-to-end retry when both nonempty `trace.md` and `answer.txt` and verified completed delivery evidence are unavailable.
- **Evaluation-only failure:** use immutable completed artifacts and measured generation evidence to retry only the judge, including timeout/invalid-JSON failures rather than only `UNREPORTED_JUDGE_TOKENS`.
- Allow **three additional retries after the initial attempt**, with a single counter per task across both modes. Immediate nested judge retries are disabled inside the suite. Stop at the first valid result, never the highest score; successful tasks are skipped on same-SHA resume.
- Preserve numbered attempt directories and all failure evidence. Report first-pass completion, recovered completion, final per-task state and attempts in the serial summary. Exhausted or accounting-blocked tasks enter `tracking-required.json` for investigation and deduplicated issue tracking; the script does not automatically publish GitHub issues.
- Evaluation recovery writes a new selected metric document and artifact hashes without overwriting original research. It includes all prior recovery usage checks; a later success cannot erase unknown spend from an intervening attempt. Valid scores remain visible even when required cost accounting still blocks the gate.
- `attempt-costs.json` separately reports known generation/judge tokens, unknown-usage counters and summed attempt wall time **including failures and retries**. It is a lower bound when usage is missing, not the comparable final-result resource aggregate. Preparation, research, judging and suite wall time are not conflated.

Only verified owned descendants are stopped, with PID start-time checks. Cleanup stays within the suite-owned inactive reconstructible environments; dataset inputs, CAS records, artifacts and evidence remain intact. Low resource checks avoid starting paid work while preserving the other task outcomes.

## Runtime fixes retained from the original candidate

- Reuse verified CAS content for unchanged workspace files only while source/CAS identities remain unchanged; mutations or tampering invalidate reuse. This avoids repeated streaming of multi-gigabyte inputs after every tool round.
- Respect configured Python package mirrors and explicit sources. Bound external environment commands to 180 seconds and pip network waits/retries, retaining gateway stall detection.
- Prefer positive provider usage aliases over zero placeholders and retain the full agent-loop usage summary rather than only the last model call.
- Keep the session title visible beside the wider full-loop token summary. Give the title a 120px flex basis so a long project name shares the available width instead of shrinking the title to zero; token accounting and unrelated journeys are unchanged.

## CI verification fixes

[Run 39754274282](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39754274282) failed only `check:research-python-ut`: its artifact records the injected paper Python 3.14, source builds of NumPy 2.2.6 / SciPy 1.15.3, and missing OpenBLAS. Fix the injected default in the shared runner while retaining the interpreter override in the research script. Validate with the same paper-3.14/gateway-3.12 combination rather than two Python-3.12 environments.

Rebased onto main `f99571df6f795d6f1b20ef248195149c9cabf836` as five linear commits, with no merge commits. Removed obsolete intermediate changes to `remote-compute-prune.test.ts` from the replayed history, retaining main's complete live-process rescan and regression fixtures throughout. The old branch could merge by final tree but could not rebase because intermediate fixture changes conflicted before being reverted. Each rewritten commit now replays cleanly on this main. Server-only ARM64 and dash-path adapters are not committed.

Restore LF in files changed by the rebase, enforce LF for workflow YAML, and restore the E2E driver's executable mode. Align the token alias fixture with main's retained conflict diagnostics, and make the harness self-test use the host's actual architecture.

Sandbox tests retain their isolation assertions while respecting the configured bubblewrap path. The shell-pruning fixture retains main's copied-bash fixture, executable-readiness checks and live-binary race regressions, and the NPU negative test uses an absent device rather than assuming the host has no Ascend cards. The skill-draft API journey explicitly loads the platform-owned skill through `read_skill`, retaining its review, publication, and file-content assertions without depending on an SDK-local import alias.

The shared runner defaults `SCIENCE_TEST_PYTHON` to the prepared gateway environment (Python 3.12, pinned by `services/gateway/.python-version`) and preserves an explicit caller override. It no longer injects the paper environment, which may use Python 3.14 and cannot install the pinned scientific wheels; the RACE contract shares that dependency-aware, no-skip driver. The harness respects an explicit `UV_CACHE_DIR`. The Evolve distribution journey supports configured PyPI mirrors and checksum-verified runtime/release-source caches while still exercising real installation, quota cancellation, sandboxed PUCT improvement, and restart reuse.

Tested commit: `9ef02324e10a888d1ffedd7469e6808075ab551f`, including main `ddebc31feef2a6e1bd1197ddb5a14ca08b6d4e38`. Full workspace build and locked dependency preparation completed. All layers used the repository's `pnpm ci:*` entry points with the PR profile and JiuwenSwarm backend.

Both the default and an explicit compatible interpreter override passed the full **4468/4468** UT layer; no skip or assertion was weakened. An unprivileged Ubuntu 26.04 container reproduces the original three shell-pruning failures; after integrating main's fixture and product fix, all **13/13** pruning tests pass, including race and unreadable-process regressions.
